title: Paula Badosa and Katerina Siniakova could collide in Guangzhou, and one has the edge
text:
Paula Badosa and Katerina Siniakova Headline Guangzhou Draw

 Guangzhou Open 2026: Paula Badosa, Daria Snigur and Katerina Siniakova Headline Draw 
 WTA Tour Guangzhou Open 2026: Paula Badosa, Daria Snigur and Katerina Siniakova Headline Draw 
 Jim Flannigan | 24 October 2026 | 3 min read Paual Badosa - Photo: IMAGO/NurPhoto Share this article
 Add us as a preferred source on Google 
 The Guangzhou Open gets underway on Monday, with former world No. 2 Paula Badosa and doubles specialist Katerina Siniakova among the biggest names in the draw. With many of the world’s top players competing in Tokyo, both have a good opportunity to challenge for the title at the WTA 250 event.
 Ukraine’s Daria Snigur is the top seed at world No. 40, with no players inside the top 40 taking part. Badosa and Siniakova have been drawn in the same half, setting up a possible semifinal meeting between the two.
 The tournament takes place from October 26 to November 1 on outdoor hard courts. A total of $283,347 in prize money is on offer, with the champion receiving $37,390 and 250 ranking points.
 Badosa Looks to Bounce Back
 Badosa, seeded fifth and ranked No. 61, opens against China’s Wang Xiyu. The Spaniard comes to Guangzhou after a disappointing first-round exit in Osaka, where she won the first set against Antonia Ruzic before losing 3-6, 6-4, 6-3.
 Her path to the quarterfinals looks manageable on paper. A win over Wang would set up a meeting with either Panna Udvardy or Sinja Kraus. Second seed Janice Tjen, who opens against Polina Kudermetova, is the most likely quarterfinal opponent.
 Badosa reached a career-high No. 2 in 2022 and has won four WTA titles, including Indian Wells in 2021. Back injuries have repeatedly slowed her career since then, but at her best she remains one of the most powerful baseliners in the field.
 Katerina Siniakova – Photo: IMAGO/NurPhoto | IMAGO/NurPhoto, IMAGO 
 Siniakova Rides Momentum
 Siniakova arrives in excellent form, but with a tight schedule. On Sunday, she plays Ashlyn Krueger in the Osaka final after beating Peyton Stearns, Magda Linette, Mary Stoiana and Katie Boulter. She then faces third seed Lanlana Tararudee in the first round in Guangzhou, a tough opener given the short turnaround.
 The Czech, ranked No. 86 before Osaka, is set for a significant rise in the rankings after this week. She has won five WTA singles titles and reached a career-high No. 27 in 2024, but she is best known as the world doubles No. 1. She has won 10 Grand Slam women’s doubles titles and has spent more than 180 weeks at the top of the doubles rankings. The two players met earlier this year in Dubai, where Badosa won in straight sets.
 Venus meets Women’s Tennis new rising star
 The draw’s most eye-catching match features fourth seed Lilli Tagger against 46-year-old Venus Williams. The seven-time Grand Slam champion is playing in Asia for the first time since 2019 and is looking to end a 15-match singles losing streak. Tagger (18) reached the quarterfinals in Osaka this week, before losing to Ann Li .
 Top seed Snigur opens against Anna Bondar, while former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin received a wild card and faces Kaitlin Quevedo. Seventh seed Maria Timofeeva and Ruzic are in Siniakova’s quarter.
